sections.text:
Petri philosophi epistula.
Petrus philosophus, cuius ἔκθεσις περὶ ἀστρονομίας in codice Neapolitano ff. 446 ss. servatur, idem esse videtur atque " Petrus diaconus et philosophus " cui excerptum de cyclo et indictione et tractatus de sideribus in codicibus Parisinis 929 (f. 97) et 3085 tribuuntur. De hoc astronomo alioquin nil comperimus (cf. Fabricius-etaneis, quae sub nomine Zoroastri prophetae circumferebantur, haec in usum suum converterit. Caput anonymum eiusdem argumenti traditur in cod. Flor. 12, saec. X, f. 123, et in cod. Mutin. 11, f. 74v. Certe divinationis methodo, quae hic adhibetur, iam antiquos Graecos usos esse comperimus ex Cicerone (cf. ad Apo-masarem, p. 124, n. 2). — De Antiocho Atheniensi, quo Hephaestio Thebanus fonte saec. V ineunte usus est (Engelbrecht, p. 36) et quem antea Porphyrius lau-daverat, vide quae congessit Boll, Sphaera, p. 54 ss. [F. C.]
sections.en:
Letter of Peter the philosopher.
Peter the philosopher, whose exposition on astronomy is preserved in the Neapolitan codex ff. 446 ff., seems to be the same as "Peter the deacon and philosopher" to whom an excerpt on the cycle and indiction and a treatise on the stars are attributed in the Parisian codices 929 (f. 97) and 3085. Otherwise we have found nothing about this astronomer (cf. Fabricius-etaneis, which were circulated under the name of the prophet Zoroaster, he converted these for his own use. An anonymous chapter of the same argument is handed down in cod. Flor. 12, 10th century, f. 123, and in cod. Mutin. 11, f. 74v. Certainly we have found from Cicero that the ancient Greeks already used the method of divination which is applied here (cf. on Apomasar, p. 124, n. 2). — Concerning Antiochus of Athens, whom Hephaestio of Thebes used as a source at the beginning of the 5th century (Engelbrecht, p. 36) and whom Porphyry had previously praised, see what Boll has collected, Sphaera, p. 54 ff. [F. C.]

summary.headline: Lunar Sign Omens
summary.text: Astrological omen list describing worldly effects when the Moon occupies each zodiac sign, including crops, rain, hail, drought, disease, earthquakes, warfare, social unrest, and the rising of the Dog Star. An editorial note identifies Peter the philosopher with Peter the deacon and philosopher and cites Neapolitan, Parisian, Florentine, and Mutinensian codices, Cicero, Antiochus of Athens, Hephaestio of Thebes, Porphyry, and Boll.
